workloads.overlap: Both model workloads stayed resident together after completion; the first successful 180-second sampler captured approximately 42 seconds of this overlap. The rebalanced run also held both roles resident; its continuous stats recorder was interrupted by deliberate Caddy recreation.

memory.before: Worker peak 1185828864 bytes left only about 21 MiB under its initial 1152 MiB limit.
memory.after: API limit reduced to 1152 MiB; worker increased to 1408 MiB; DB384/frontend384/Caddy96 retained. Repeated OCR plus embeddings passed with worker peak1225428992 bytes.

cpu.reason: Docker stats reports percentages incompatible with verified CPU quotas/cpuset on this emulated VM (for example PostgreSQL exceeds its 0.5-core quota). These values are not a certified native CPU measurement. Use host-side raw /proc and cgroup rate profiling during AWS E2E.

sampling.sampler_fix: Checkpoint new run identity; retain Docker-stats replacement/timeout errors explicitly without substituting zero usage. Two focused regression tests passed.

limitations: Linux x86_64 execution was emulated; native AWS CPU/latency must be measured.
The workload uses small synthetic PDFs and bounded embedding/reranking batches; it does not certify sustained adversarial 25 MB/100-page concurrent uploads.
Synthetic model profiles add processes inside idle service containers. The ordinary indexing queue was kept idle until those processes exited; subsequent browser tests used only the normal worker.

A transient documents503 was observed under the initial concurrency4/keepalive5 deployment; the lead changed keepalive to0 while retaining concurrency4; final native/browser follow-up belongs to the lead.
